_doc: ADR-551 · Resource guardrails. The ONE policy for disk/memory thresholds, process classes, heavy-job admission and allow-listed cleanup. Read by spa_core/monitoring/resource_guard.py and spa_core/utils/heavy_job.py. Changing a number here is a reviewed commit, not a runtime knob. Canonical, git-tracked; nothing here is a financial or risk limit.

disk._why: Measured 2026-10-02/03: the Data volume reached 0 bytes twice (ENOSPC 22:58-23:03Z and 07:55-08:05Z) from ~87 GB of abandoned test stands plus parallel worktrees; nothing in the fleet asked «is there room to write». 15 GB still lets the alert itself be written. The reserve file is released at CRITICAL so canonical writers (paper books, atomic_save) keep room while the cause is found. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-10-29 (ADR-862): this _why used to justify warn_free_gb=40 as «a day of the worst measured growth (~30 GB/day)». That premise is FALSE by a measured x14.3 — on 2026-10-29 a single agent log (/tmp/spa_decision_loop.log, com.spa.decision_loop) grew 17.87 GB/h = 428.9 GB/day, so 40 GB is 2.2 HOURS of headroom and 15 GB is 50 minutes, not a day and half a day. The levels are NOT raised here: a level cannot notice its own premise going stale, and raising it would only move the same blind line. The rate below is what noticed. Cause of that growth is owner-gated (owner-decision-disk-snova-sel-odin-zhurnal-agenta-9-82): the three fixes are money-path, risk logic and an agent restart.

exhaustion._why: ADR-862. The guard ran every 5 minutes for a month publishing only the LEVEL, so the rate had to be timed by hand with a sleep loop by two sessions in a row (#978, #979) and the owner's card said «about 28 minutes» when the measured answer was 33. min_span_s=240 because the guard's own interval is 300 s and a span shorter than that is jitter, not a rate; max_span_s=7200 because a sample older than two hours says nothing about now (the guard may have been down between them) — past it the verdict is WARMING_UP, never a stale rate. max_samples=24 keeps two hours of 5-minute history. critical_minutes_to_full=60 fires at 18 GB free under the growth measured on 2026-10-29 — an hour BEFORE the 15 GB level line, which is the whole point of measuring a rate. These are not financial or risk limits; changing them is a reviewed commit, like every other number in this file.

memory._why: kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level: 1 normal, 2 warn, 4 critical (the kernel's own grading, not ours). Swap on this Mac is 3 x 1 GB files; the previous Claude session's wait loops were killed under low memory on 2026-10-02/03.

CRITICAL._why: Derived from dependencies: the paper books (hy/lp sleeves, the daily Conservative cycle) are the canonical writers the package status read model reads (spa_core/defi_engine/package_status.py); the site and Director read that model through the API (com.spa.apiserver) behind the tunnel (com.spa.cloudflared). A lost run here is a lost observation that cannot be backfilled.

IMPORTANT._why: Owner surfaces (Director, the Mission Control cockpit — mission_server/mission_control, added 2026-10-16 ADR-763: they ran UNCLASSIFIED although they are the live cockpit; the older director_server/director_build are still loaded and stay listed —, Telegram), the backup that keeps evidence off-host, Trading Research (must not break), the health and resource monitors themselves, and the autonomous build loop runner (its CHILDREN are disposable, the scheduler is not). RTMR sense loop (ADR-053) feeds the Conservative book's FREEZE reaction.

DISPOSABLE._why: Test shards, headless LLM runs, browser verification and anything executing from a disposable /tmp worktree. They may be slowed (nice) under pressure; they are never killed by the guard.

heavy_jobs._why: docs/audits/p0-ci-resource-admission.md: two concurrent full runs drove free memory to 0.1 GB and six jobs were killed. A full suite takes a lease; a third waits; the same tree is never claimed by two live jobs.

disposable_dirs._why: mkdtemp stands of measurement tools and tests (ADR-546: 957 g17_/g18_ dirs, 87 GB). Created by code, never canonical.
Test backup stands (spa_test_backups_*). Headless-browser profiles were dropped from the list: a short prefix (vpsys…) could match another tool's directory (review 2026-10-03).

worktrees._why: Linked git worktrees are removed ONLY by the existing reaper: idle >= 24 h, every changed path delivered/superseded, archived to ~/SPA_backups/worktree_reap before removal; anything unproven stays.
